task.text: Implement `Reactor`: wait for ready events, then dispatch each to the handler registered for its operation.
`Events.java` is given (`Op`, `Ready`, `Demultiplexer`, `Handler`); do not edit it.

items: `Reactor(Demultiplexer)`, and `on(Op, Handler)` returns the reactor; a later handler for the same `Op` replaces the earlier one.
`run()` calls `select()` repeatedly and dispatches each batch in order, on the calling thread, until `select()` returns an empty list.
`stop()` ends `run()` once the current batch is dispatched.
An event whose `Op` has no handler throws `IllegalStateException` naming the `Op`.
Handlers may call `on` during dispatch; later events see it. Look handlers up in a registry: no `switch` or `if` per `Op`.

checks.title: run ends on an empty batch
A new handler replaces the old one
An unhandled Op is an error
Handlers run on the caller's thread
stop finishes the batch, then ends
A handler can register more handlers
Dispatch is a lookup, not branches
Handlers live in a private final Map

hints.text: A reactor separates three jobs: waiting for readiness (the `Demultiplexer`), choosing a handler, and the handler's work. The loop knows nothing about what an operation means, only which handler is registered for it.

Keep a private final `EnumMap<Op, Handler>`. `run()` loops: ask `demux.select()`, stop on an empty list or when a `stopped` flag is set, otherwise look up `handlers.get(event.op())` for each event in the batch.
